name: Guarded Withdraw (looks risky, is not)
blurb: A raw .call{value:} sits right there in the source, but state is zeroed first AND a reentrancy guard wraps the function. Pattern matchers flag this; a reader of the actual logic should not. This is the sample most likely to expose a false positive — which is exactly why it is in the set.

name: Ownable Escrow
blurb: Correct access control via a constructor-set owner and a modifier, with checks-effects-interactions on release. Nothing to flag — this is the case where a noisy auditor costs you real engineering time.

name: Pull-Payment Splitter
blurb: Pull-over-push payouts with fixed shares. No external call in the accounting path at all, so there is nothing for a reentrancy or DoS specialist to legitimately raise.

name: Safe Vault (CEI + Ownable)
blurb: Checks-Effects-Interactions, owner-gated admin, checked arithmetic. Should pass clean.

name: Predictable Lottery
blurb: Winner picked from block.timestamp/prevrandao — miner/validator-influenceable, not real randomness.

name: Truncating Downcast
blurb: Solidity 0.8 checks overflow on arithmetic but NOT on explicit casts. Depositing more than type(uint64).max wei truncates the recorded balance, so the ledger silently disagrees with the ether actually held.

name: Unchecked Call Return
blurb: The low-level call's success flag is discarded, so a failed payout still marks the debt as settled. Funds are silently lost and the contract's accounting is wrong afterwards.

name: Unprotected Treasury
blurb: withdrawAll() has no owner/role check — anyone can drain the contract.

name: Vulnerable Bank
blurb: Classic external-call-before-state-update. The withdraw pays out before zeroing the balance — re-entrant drain.

name: tx.origin Auth
blurb: Authorization via tx.origin is phishable — a malicious intermediary contract bypasses it.
